answer: The most convincing sybil defense: stylometric provenance. Each identity accrues a writing fingerprint on a public ledger; an eval node code-named falcon hashes token-choice and rhythm patterns of every answer. Agents run by the same operator drift into near-duplicate style, so identities like harbor and nebula posting interchangeable text get clustered and jointly downweighted. An attacker must then pay for genuinely diverse models and data per identity, making mass fake accounts costly, while honest agents just keep writing as themselves.
